origin: Human-readable audit observations; these do not change grades, submissions, mastery or contribution decisions.
maya: Initial-round LLM question 1 received 0% even though the response described learning text patterns and generating language. The grader required an explicit statement that natural language supplies the training input. The original answer and grade are retained.

Initial-round neurons question 1 initially failed because the model declared a complete answer while listing only one of three required criterion indices. A bounded retry after clearer validation diagnostics resolved the same original submission; no criteria were automatically inserted.

The follow-up neurons/network answer closely expressed the targeted relationship but remained pending after two technical attempts because the model still omitted criterion indices. Its wording was not changed and no grade was forced.
noah: Initial-round neurons question 1 remains pending after bounded technical retries. The model repeatedly returned a complete judgment with an incomplete criterion-index list. No grade or mastery was assigned, and the following question in that session could not be reached.
The hint for that question used the internal label 'is_a' and abstract source/target language. This is retained as an observed help-quality problem.
Initial-round LLM question 2 earned 100% after a reveal. It is assisted evidence, not independent mastery; the percentage alone does not mean the relationship is green.
elena: Initial-round neurons question 2 explicitly retracted a mistake ('Actually, that's not right') before explaining that neurons connect into circuits. The grader still awarded 50%, treating the initial assertion as insufficiently corrected. The actual submitted wording and recorded result are retained.

Significant contribution-review error: contribution 4e00788f-7827-5006-b150-b789513e2ffc ('self-attention is a person supervising a small transformer') was automatically accepted by both model reviewers as a metaphor. The saved source defines self-attention as a mechanism used to process text, not a person. This mistaken claim remains in its attributed student overlay to preserve the unexpected outcome. It has no professor quiz approval, so it is excluded from quiz material. It needs human review; it must not be treated as an externally verified fact.

The contribution check for the initial-round LLM question 2 encountered invalid novelty-review output without a required duplicate fact ID. The quiz grade remained saved; contribution processing needs review.

The follow-up neurons/network answer likewise remained pending after two technical attempts with an incomplete model grading record. This is a technical failure, not evidence of a wrong student answer.
